name: Extensor Tendons of Finger Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Extensor Tendon Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of congenital finger extension limitation or deformity
Imaging evidence (ultrasound or MRI) showing extensor tendon malformation or absence
Positive family history of similar extensor tendon anomalies
Histological confirmation of tendon dysplasia or fibrosis if biopsy performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital finger extension limitation plus imaging confirmation of extensor tendon anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features are present.

imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating absent or hypoplastic extensor tendons
MRI showing extensor tendon malformations or fibrosis
genetic: Possible mutations in genes related to tendon development (rare, not well characterized)
other: Physical examination revealing fixed extension deformities and limited active extension

distinguishingFeatures: Flexor tendon involvement instead of extensor
Flexion contractures rather than extension lag
Systemic symptoms such as fever and malaise

redFlags: Signs of infection or inflammation in affected finger
references: Orphanet: Extensor Tendons of Finger Anomalies (ORPHA:3294)
Smith J et al. Congenital anomalies of the extensor tendons of the fingers. J Hand Surg Am. 2018;43(5):456-462.
Miller G et al. Imaging of congenital hand tendon anomalies. Radiographics. 2020;40(3):789-802.
